data.long_meaning: Derived from the French name ‘Manon’, which originated from the Hebrew name ‘Emmanu’ meaning ‘God with us’. This name is commonly used in Christianity and has a rich history associated with various saints. The name Manon carries the meaning “Little One” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Manon usually hope their child will grow to embody little one and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: מאנון
in_hebrew.meaning: מאנון משמעות היא ביטוי של משאלה או תפילה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם מאנון נגזר מהעברית ומשמעותו קשורה לביטוי של משאלה או תפילה. הוא מורכב משורשים עבריים הקשורים למושגים של משאלה ותקווה. השם מאנון משמש כביטוי של אמונה ותקווה באלוהים.

in_greek.name: Μανών
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Μανών έχει τις ρίζες του στην ελληνική γλώσσα και σχετίζεται με την έννοια της ευχής ή της παράκλησης. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, παρόμοια ονόματα συνδέονται με έννοιες πνευματικές και θρησκευτικές. Το όνομα Μανών αντανακλά την πνευματική σχέση με το θείο.

in_english.name: Manon
in_english.long_meaning: The name Manon is derived from Hebrew origins, specifically from the name 'Miryam' or 'Mary', which means 'bitter'. It is also associated with the French name 'Manon', meaning 'wished-for child'. In Christian tradition, Manon symbolizes a child born out of prayer and desire. The name carries a rich history and spiritual significance across various cultures.

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Manon' has been popularized in various cultures, especially in European literature and art. The most notable is the Novel "Manon Lescaut" by Abbé Prévost, which tells the story of a beautiful and seductive woman named Manon who leaves her religious order to live a life of passion and luxury, eventually facing tragic consequences. In musical circles, the opera "Manon" by Massenet is one of the most enduring works, continuing to captivate audiences with its powerful and moving story.
data.spiritual_significance: The name 'Manon' carries a deep spiritual significance in Christian tradition. It is derived from the Hebrew name ‘Emmanu’, meaning ‘God with us’. This name emphasizes the belief that God is always present in our lives and provides us with divine guidance and protection. By choosing the name 'Manon', parents can remind their child of the comforting presence of God, encouraging them to live a life rooted in faith and trust.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Manon is derived from the Hebrew name "Emmanu'el," meaning "God with us." In Christian tradition, Manon represents the divine presence and God's unwavering love accompanying a person throughout their life.

historical_references.reference: Manon Lescaut, a tragic opera by Danish composer Jules Massenet, based on Abbé Prévost's novel ‘L'Histoire du Chevalier des Grieux et de Manon Lescaut’ from 1731.
historical_references.context: Massenet's opera, first performed in 1884, is considered one of the greatest love stories in opera. The novel is an epistolary novel, told through letters.

historical_references.reference: Manon de la Tour, a character in Mark Twain's novel ‘A Connecticut Yankee in King Arthur's Court’, published in 1889. In this novel, Manon is a beautiful serving girl at King Arthur's court.
historical_references.context: Twain's Manon is a major character in his satirical novel and is known for her beauty and her ingenuity in helping the protagonist, Hank Morgan, adjust to medieval life.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Christian name 'Manon' has seen a modern resurgence in various forms of media and entertainment. It is a popular name in French literature, particularly in the novel 'Manon Lescaut' by Abbé Prévost. In the Opera world, there are numerous productions of the opera 'Manon' based on the novel. Lastly, in the realm of Romance novels, the name Manon is used in various titles and plots, appealing to readers who enjoy historical and romantic stories.
